Manchester Crown Court was told he had also encouraged his staff to cover up his dishonesty by selling goods with false safety approval markings. Judge Timothy Smith sentenced Harrison to 175 hours of unpaid work alongside the suspended jail sentence. 'Deliberate and dishonest' He also disqualified the him from being a company director for eight years. "You were prepared to invite staff, including your own son, to lie and hide your own conduct and regulatory failings. "You have lost your good name and reputation." Harrison's firm sold feeding pumps which were used in neonatal intensive care units and special care baby units to feed very sick newborn babies directly into their stomachs. title: Bakery owner calls for Budget help for firms

input.lead: Frankie Dyer has written to the prime minister urging Budget support for businesses
input.summary: Frankie Dyer has written to the prime minister urging Budget support for businesses
input.evidence_text: The owner of a bakery in Manchester has urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham to give the hospitality industry a 'fighting chance' as it struggles to keep up with increasing prices Barbakan Deli is an artisan bakery and deli in Chorlton that has been at the heart of the community for the last 62 years. However, it is struggling to keep up with its bills, despite turning over more than £2.3m a year In an open letter to the prime minister, owner Frankie Dyer said there is "nowhere left to squeeze" and asked for independent businesses to be considered in the upcoming Budget A Treasury spokesperson said decisions on tax are "a matter for the Chancellor to set out at fiscal events" In the letter, which has since been widely seen by nearly a million people online, Dyer wrote: "Since Covid, independent businesses like ours have dragged ourselves through crisis after crisis." "Energy prices. Fuel costs. Food shortages. Inflation. Increasing wages. Pension contributions. Corporation Tax at 25%. Business rates. And then the enormous additional cost of the increase in Employer National Insurance."

title: Middleton residents campaign to keep beloved kickpitch

input.lead: Residents in the Langley Estate of Middleton are campaigning to keep their community kickpitch in the area
input.summary: Residents in the Langley Estate of Middleton are campaigning to keep their community kickpitch in the area
input.evidence_text: Residents in Middleton are campaigning for a replacement football pitch after plans were announced to turn the existing site into a car park Campaigners say the pitch in Burnside Crescent on the Langley Estate is a community hub as well as somewhere people can play football and other sports The pitch, which is next to the Burnside Centre, is one of three on the estate, and the car park will be for the centre Families say they have been told replacement facilities will be provided at Rochdale AFC and Rochdale Council's planned Football and Community Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee Playing Fields. But they are campaigning for the new pitch to be created on land next to the original The Burnside Centre said it understands why people are disappointed to see the pitch decommissioned, but said one of the reasons the decision was made related to concerns about antisocial behaviour It added: "The pitch, which dates back to the late 1990s, had reached the end of its expected lifespan and required significant investment to remain operational."

input.evidence_text: The need for invasive post-mortems across Rochdale, Bury, and Oldham could be reduced by up to 80 per cent thanks to pioneering new digital autopsies The innovative service is being delivered by the Coroner’s Office for Greater Manchester, in partnership with the NHS, specialist post-mortem imaging provider Anubix, and medical imaging provider TIC Health Working with pathologists, radiologists and mortuary staff at the Northern Care Alliance the coroner’s office will, where appropriate, provide computed tomography (CT) scanning to help inform a person’s cause of death Teams will use post-mortem imaging to check if a cause of death can be determined without the need for traditional invasive post-mortems, a process that can cause further distress to relatives during the grieving process A number of scans a week will be carried out using the new technology, with a long-term ambition of speeding up the service provided for relatives following the loss of a loved one Councillor Neil Emmott, leader of Rochdale Borough Council, said

input.evidence_text: Stoptober is back, encouraging smokers across Bolton to take the first step towards a healthier, smokefree future The national NHS campaign challenges smokers to quit for 28 days in October, with evidence showing that people who remain smokefree for four weeks are five times more likely to quit for good Smokers are being encouraged to access Bolton's free community stop smoking service, where they can receive 12 weeks of free behavioural support, personalised advice and evidence-based quit aids, including nicotine replacement therapies, vaping kits and stop smoking medication Stopping smoking is one of the best things people can do for their health, with benefits beginning almost immediately Every year, thousands of people successfully quit and reduce their risk of serious illnesses such as cancer, heart disease and respiratory disease Smoking rates have fallen significantly in recent years, showing that more people are choosing a smokefree life

input.evidence_text: Thousands of illicit cigarettes, tobacco and unsafe children's toys were seized by Bolton Council during Operation Avro, a multi-agency day of action Trading standards officers joined colleagues from Greater Manchester Police, Immigration Enforcement, and specialist dog handlers from Wagtails on Thursday September 17, to carry out targeted inspections of businesses across the borough A total of nine premises were visited, and officers seized around 12,000 counterfeit and non-duty paid cigarettes, half a kilogram of hand-rolling tobacco and more than 500 "squishy" toys that failed to meet UK safety standards The estimated value of the goods seized exceeds £14,500 and investigations are ongoing The operation formed part of Greater Manchester's Operation Avro initiative, which brings together a range of partners to tackle crime, protect communities and target illegal activity Councillor Akhtar Zaman, Leader of Bolton Council, said

input.evidence_text: The new exhibition Laura Knight: The Art of Community opens at Bolton Museum on Saturday 19 September The exhibition brings together the museum’s small but significant collection of works by the pioneering British artist This is the first time that the four paintings and one drawing have been shown together in one gallery Dame Laura Knight (1877-1970) is one of Britain’s best-loved artists whose career spanned 70 years and encompassed a huge variety of subjects, techniques, and styles Her achievements were many: she was the first female artist to be elected as a full member of the Royal Academy, she was a prominent war artist in both World Wars, and she was made a Dame in 1929 for her services to art The exhibition at Bolton Museum includes her celebrated painting, The Fishing Fleet , from 1900, with the dramatic work depicting the working life of the fishing community in Staithes

input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
